candidates: In Playwright e2e test files, always `await` every async Playwright operation—both action methods (e.g., `.click()`, `.fill()`, `.check()`) and `expect()` assertions. Omitting `await` causes race conditions or silent test failures. Also ensure every assertion statement is terminated with a semicolon, not a comma; a trailing comma converts the assertion into an unevaluated expression that silently never executes.

When asserting the enabled/disabled state of native HTML form elements (`<button>`, `<input>`, `<select>`, etc.), use jest-dom's `toBeEnabled()` and `toBeDisabled()` matchers rather than `toHaveAttribute('aria-disabled', 'true')`, because native elements use the `disabled` HTML attribute, not `aria-disabled`. Reserve `toHaveAttribute('aria-disabled', 'true')` for custom interactive elements that deliberately use the ARIA attribute to convey disabled state while remaining keyboard-focusable (as is the convention in this project's `Button` component).
